sections.heading: You Deal With the Owner
body: Get three quotes for the same windows and you can end up with three very different prices. It's hard to know who is quoting the job and who is quoting the commission.
When the owner quotes the job, nobody is paid to upsell you. I come out, look at what you have, explain your options in plain words and give you a price. You decide on your own time.
The person who gave you the price is the person you call if you have a question. That's how a small company works when the owner is the one on the phone.

sections.heading: Windows Are What We Do Most
body: Most people call us about a window that stopped doing its job. A room that never gets comfortable. A sash that sticks or won't stay up.
Or fog between the panes, or traffic you can hear as if the window were open.
Fog and noise usually mean the seal has failed. Once it does, the window leaks air and noise no matter how clean the glass looks. You pay to heat and cool the street through it.

We replace double-hung, sliding, casement, picture, awning, shaped and basement windows. They're custom-built double-pane windows with Low-E glass and argon gas between the panes, made to fit your openings.
Replace one window, a few, or every window in the house. People do all three, and some come back for the rest once they see the first ones.

sections.heading: How You Know a Window Is Done
body: Some windows fail loudly. A sash that sticks, a crank that spins without moving anything, a window that won't stay up on its own.
Most fail quietly. The room never gets comfortable, you feel a draft on your hand at the glass, or you hear the road as if the window were open.

Fog between the panes is the clearest sign. A double-pane window is two sheets of glass with sealed air or gas between them. When the seal fails, that space fills with moist air and the window stops insulating.
After that, cleaning won't help. The glass unit has to be replaced, and on an older window the frame usually has worn out along with it.

sections.heading: Window Styles, and Where Each One Fits
body: We replace double-hung, sliding, casement, picture, awning and shaped windows, and basement windows too. The right style depends on the opening and how you use the room.

**Double-hung** windows slide up and down and suit most older homes. **Sliders** slide side to side, which works for wide, short openings and basements. **Casements** crank outward on a hinge and press tight against the frame when closed.

**Picture windows** don't open at all, which means fewer parts to fail and more glass for the view. **Awning windows** hinge at the top, so you can leave them open in the rain. **Shaped windows** fill the odd openings, the arches and angles that a standard window won't fit.
Some openings are harder than others. Rick works out what fits instead of telling you it can't be done.

sections.heading: What Goes Into Our Windows
body: Our windows are custom-built double-pane windows with double-strength glass, a Low-E coating and argon gas between the panes. They exceed ENERGY STAR qualification criteria.
Low-E is a thin coating that reflects heat. It keeps your furnace heat inside in January and the sun's heat out in July. The argon between the panes slows heat down more than plain air does.
Replace one window, a few, or every window in the house. You don't have to do it all at once, and plenty of people start with the worst rooms and come back for the rest.

sections.heading: Why a Door Wears Out
body: A door opens and closes thousands of times a year, and the weather works on it from the outside the whole time.
The weatherstripping flattens and lets air through. The threshold at the bottom takes the water and, over the years, rots. The hinges loosen and the door sags until it rubs the frame.
On a patio slider, the rollers wear and the track bends. That's why you end up shoving the door open with your shoulder.
A new door in a good frame fixes the cause. Adjusting an old door fixes the symptom for a season.

sections.heading: Can a Door Be Fixed Instead?
body: Sometimes. If the door itself is sound and only the weatherstripping is tired, new seals may be all it needs.
Replace it when the threshold or frame has rotted, when the door has warped so it won't latch, or when a slider's track is bent. Those problems come back no matter how many times you adjust the door.
Rick looks at it with you and tells you which one you have. If the door is worth keeping, he says so.

sections.heading: The Doors We Install
body: We install entry, patio, French and side doors. They're custom-manufactured, so they're made for your opening instead of pulled from a shelf.
**Entry doors** are the front of the house. The door, the frame and the seal around it decide how much of the draft you feel in the hall.
**Patio doors** are the biggest opening most houses have, and the leakiest when old. **French doors** swing on hinges and give you the wide opening with a tighter seal than an old slider.
**Side doors** get less attention, and they get a lot of use. A swollen side door that you slam every summer is worth replacing, not planing.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn what you do and where.
problems: On a phone the page is twice as wide as the screen. Your number and half your menu sit past the edge, so callers scroll sideways to find you.
The top of the page is three headlines: windows, hail roofing claims, and Wichita. Google can't tell whether you're a window company or a roofer.
"Here's what our customers are saying..." has nothing under it and you're never named, so visitors miss the praise that wins you jobs.
fixes: Your number one tap away, with the whole menu on screen.
A headline that says exterior remodeling company in Wichita, KS.
You introduced as the owner, in your own voice, with a real review beside each point.
cards.alsoAdd: On day one, we sit down with you to get what makes you the obvious choice, every service you offer and every town you work in. That becomes the prescription: how many pages, in how many towns, so Google and AI tools can find you for every service.

Styles, glass, install steps and payment, each beside a real review.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

onboardingQuestions: How does Rick Timsah want to be introduced on the site (owner, general manager), and who is the "Dan" in the company name? No person named Dan is confirmed, so the site never mentions one.
Real business hours: the current site says Monday to Friday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Birdeye says 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Hours are left off the demo until confirmed.
Which email address should customers use? The current site shows contact@ddtrm.com. It is not in our verified facts, so the demo shows no email.

What does the warranty cover and for how long? The old site says an exclusive lifetime warranty and a 3-year glass breakage warranty; Rick's reply to one review says his warranty covers the installation. The demo says only that the warranty covers the installation.

Which window brand does Rick install today? The old site links a ProVia warranty PDF and lists Pro-Via and Quaker windows, but ProVia's dealer locator did not list the company, so no brand is named. Are the windows still custom-built and American-made?

Licenses and certifications to verify, with numbers: Kansas lead-based renovator (KDHE), Class B building contractor, Kansas licensed roofer, and Owens Corning. Is the company insured? None of it appears on the demo.
Years in business: the earliest Google review is 2018 and Rick's reply to a 2025 review says over 12 years. What founding year can we use?

Full list of services to confirm: gutters, basement and picture windows, roofing and hail claims, metal buildings, Smart Lap and concrete siding, aluminum window and door wraps, garage doors, storm doors, window repair.
Do they want roofing and hail damage claims on the new site, and should the (833) 972-ROOF number show? The demo shows it as the roofing line on the homepage and contact page.

Showroom: is it open to walk-ins during business hours, or by appointment?
Legal business name, logo file and brand colors. Who controls the dandanthewindowman.com domain (the site is a Hibu build)?
